intent_en: To explain a financial gap by contrasting the share of profits spent on stock buybacks among GM, Toyota, and Volkswagen.
previous_intent: To explain a gap between major automakers by contrasting their stock buyback practices, showing that GM spends a large portion of profits while Volkswagen has spent none since 2012 and Toyota's spending is much lower.
narration_support: And you can see part of the reason for this gap when you look at how much of their profits these three companies spend on buybacks.
chart_support: Line chart titled 'Share of profits spent on stock buybacks' from 2012 to 2017, showing GM with high values, Toyota with lower values, and Volkswagen flat at the baseline.
evidence_note: The narration explicitly links the chart data to explaining a 'gap' and compares the three companies' buyback behaviors. The chart visualizes this with GM having high fluctuating values, Toyota having moderate values, and Volkswagen remaining flat at the bottom (0% share) throughout the period.
